firstScreen.notes: 1440-first.jpg: h1 'Atlanta flooring with the wear layer on the quote' names trade + city + promise in 2 lines; a proof line sits under it (Sample 4.8 from 231 reviews, open until 5 pm); Compare floors primary + outlined Call; phone in header; the proof band now peeks at 845px. The result appears once (dark LVP chip + one reason line). 390-first.jpg: h1 3 lines, proof line and both buttons above the fold, sticky Call/Compare bar. Not higher: the left half of the 1440 hero has a large empty block above the h1 while the right half is a dense tool, so the two columns don't balance.

distinctiveness.notes: The sample-chip system runs through the hero tool (1440-first.jpg), the four floor cards with layer swatches, the peeling cross-section story (1440-scroll-25.jpg), the RH probe drawing (1440-scroll-50.jpg), the cut-corner review cards (1440-scroll-75.jpg), the estimator chip strip, the route map and the deep footer (1440-rm-full.jpg). The tracked-caps micro-labels are gone from the hero. Not higher: the bone + terracotta palette is still close to sibling flooring/A's cream + rust.

type.notes: 1440-first.jpg: tight heavy Archivo h1, comfortable Karla lede, DM Mono kept to spec values (12 mil wear, SPC core), and sentence-case labels replace the tracked caps. 1440-scroll-25.jpg: the story lines are now Karla with bold layer names, not centred mono. 1440-scroll-75.jpg: italic review quotes at two sizes give hierarchy. Not higher: the mono spec text in the hero cards (letter-spaced 'Ply core', 'Refinishable') is small and light at 1440.

layout.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg: the services split into 4 featured floor cards plus a 'Prep, repair and stairs' list, which removes the uniform 10-chip grid; reviews alternate narrow/wide cards (1440-scroll-75.jpg); the contact section is now two columns; the tones alternate paper/mid/deep/paper/plank/mid/accent/deep/paper/deep. Not higher: in 1440-scroll-50.jpg the slab checklist ends at 560px and leaves a dead right column beside the probe drawing; the story stage (1440-scroll-25.jpg) has large empty dark fields above and below the diagram.

photo.notes: No raster photos (placeholders withdrawn); judged on the drawn treatments. The edge-on plank band, RH probe drawing (1440-scroll-50.jpg), cross-section layers (1440-scroll-25.jpg), floor-card swatches and Atlanta route sketch (1440-rm-full.jpg) share one palette and one hand. Nothing is blank or broken, and the round-4 triangle artefact is gone. Not 9: the drawings are diagrams rather than material; nothing shows the texture of oak, tile or LVP at a size a buyer would feel.

copy.notes: 1440-first.jpg: the lede earns the concept ('so three quotes finally line up side by side'); the result line gives a plain reason. 1440-scroll-50.jpg: 'Your slab has a number. We read it first.' with concrete bullets. 1440-scroll-75.jpg: reviews carry specific stories (1960s ranch dip, gray that looked green at four o'clock), all labelled Sample review. Card links now read 'Price this floor' with no arrow. Not higher: the action still has three names (Compare floors / Price this floor / Price my floor, 1440-rm-full.jpg).

mobile.notes: 390-first.jpg: the h1 is 3 lines, the proof line and both actions sit above the fold, the sticky bar has thumb-size targets, and the room pills wrap cleanly. 390-rm-full.jpg: floor cards stack, the story is unpinned with the diagram under the text, the reviews are single column, and the estimator and form stack. 390-full.jpg shows the lower bands unrevealed in a full-page capture, a stitching artefact that the rm shot clears. Not higher: the services run is still long on the phone.

a11y.notes: Round-4 contrast failures fixed: --muted is now #5E5046/#5C4F44 on the light bands (about 6:1) and the footer paints deep (1440-rm-full.jpg bottom). Reduced-motion shots show all content (1440-rm-full.jpg, 390-rm-full.jpg). Checkboxes, ZIP and form fields have visible labels (1440-scroll-50.jpg). static.json clean. Not higher: the dimmed inactive story lines (1440-scroll-25.jpg, 'Print film', 'Rigid core') read low against the dark field while pinned.

motion.notes: 1440-scroll-25.jpg: the wear layer has physically lifted off the print film and core, its label is drawn beside it, and the matching text line is lit while the others dim, so the peel now explains the 12 mil. The hero compare chips drive the result card (1440-first.jpg), and the estimator strip fills with the slider (1440-rm-full.jpg). Not higher: only one layer label is visible at 25%, and the frames don't show the print film and core getting labelled in turn.

wow.notes: 1440-first.jpg: kitchen + pets + slab -> LVP, 12 mil wear, SPC core, shown as a real sample chip with a reason. Backed by the slab checklist with the RH probe drawing (1440-scroll-50.jpg) and the chip-strip estimator with a printable price (1440-rm-full.jpg). A homeowner would use it, and a contractor would want it. Not 10: the moments are smart tools rather than one unforgettable image.

polish.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg: the footer is now a deep, designed close with the TM chip and nav strip; cut corners repeat on hero cards, reviews and slab panel; rules are one weight; and the stray plank triangle is gone. Not higher: the Sample badges are mustard pills while the hero 'Sample' tag is square, so the radius is not chosen once (1440-first.jpg vs 1440-scroll-75.jpg).

elevate.move: Make the material the image: one large drawn or macro plank-end study per floor in the services cards (oak growth rings, tile body, LVP film stack), so the cards show what you stand on and not just a swatch icon.
Anchor the h1 to the top of the hero and let the chip tool rise as one stacked sample board beside it, so both columns start on the same line and the result chip is the visual climax of the fold.
